gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each dock costs per watt of laptop charging from its own power brick. The AV Access iDock C20 charges two laptops at 60 W each, 120 W in total, for $259.99 ($2.17/W). The Sabrent SB-TB4K gives 60 W for $299.99 ($5.00/W). The TESmart HDC202-X24 gives 60 W for $699 ($11.65/W). The AV Access KD-E10's own 36 W adapter does not charge the laptop at all: you still need the laptop's charger.
standout_why: I read four rival pages. Three are cited by ChatGPT: dockgearhq built-in-KVM docks (2026), dockgearhq dual-monitor KVMs (2026) and avaccess.com best-kvm-switches. The fourth, thunderboltlaptop.com dual-monitor KVMs, appeared in ChatGPT's first chat. The dockgearhq pages and thunderboltlaptop already add up combined charging (C20 120 W, StarTech 135 W, Cable Matters/Anker 130 W). None of them prints a price, and dockgearhq and thunderboltlaptop both say cost per watt can't be worked out. None says that the KD-E10's bundled adapter is only 12 V 3 A and can't power the laptop. None quotes TESmart's warning that laptops without 20 V charging may get only 7.5 W.
decides: For two laptops, this backs the iDock C20 as the value pick. It gives the most laptop charging per dollar among the four picks I could price, and it charges both laptops at once from one 200 W brick. It also weakens the case for the KD-E10 as 'best value for laptop + desktop', because the shopper still needs the laptop's own charger. It shows the $699 TESmart pays about 5× more per charging watt than the C20, for one laptop at 60 W.
